title: MATH GAOKAO - 413
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate simple interest using the formula \(I=Prt\).
questions.question: A bank offers a simple interest rate of \(6\%\) per year. If \(5000\text{ USD}\) is deposited for \(4\) years, how much interest is earned?
questions.explanation:
Use the simple interest formula \(I=Prt\). Here \(P=5000\), \(r=0.06\), and \(t=4\). Thus
\[
I=5000\cdot0.06\cdot4=1200.
\]
So the interest earned is \(1200\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Use the simple interest formula \(I=Prt\), where \(P\) is principal, \(r\) is annual rate, and \(t\) is time in years.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the amount under annual compound interest.
questions.question: An investment of \(2000\text{ USD}\) earns \(5\%\) interest compounded annually. What is the amount after \(2\) years?
questions.explanation:
The compound amount formula is \(A=P(1+r)^t\). With \(P=2000\), \(r=0.05\), and \(t=2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=2000(1.05)^2 \\
&=2000(1.1025) \\
&=2205.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the amount after \(2\) years is \(2205\text{ USD}\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the present value of a future amount under compound discounting.
questions.question: What is the present value of \(8000\text{ USD}\) due in \(3\) years if the annual interest rate is \(6\%\) compounded annually? Round to the nearest cent.
questions.explanation:
The present value is
\[
\text{PV}=\frac{A}{(1+r)^t}.
\]
Here \(A=8000\), \(r=0.06\), and \(t=3\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{PV}&=\frac{8000}{(1.06)^3} \\
&=\frac{8000}{1.191016} \\
&\approx6716.95.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the present value is approximately \(6716.95\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Discount the future amount by dividing by \((1+r)^t\).

questions.concept: Future Value of an Ordinary Annuity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the future value of equal annual deposits.
questions.question: A student deposits \(1000\text{ USD}\) at the end of each year for \(5\) years into an account earning \(4\%\) annual interest compounded annually. What is the future value of these deposits immediately after the fifth deposit? Round to the nearest cent.
questions.explanation:
Use the future value formula for an ordinary annuity:
\[
\text{FV}=\text{PMT}\frac{(1+r)^t-1}{r}.
\]
Here \(\text{PMT}=1000\), \(r=0.04\), and \(t=5\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{FV}&=1000\frac{(1.04)^5-1}{0.04} \\
&=1000\frac{0.2166529024}{0.04} \\
&\approx5416.32.
\end{aligned}
\]
So the future value is approximately \(5416.32\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Use the ordinary annuity future value formula with payments at the end of each period.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the annual compound interest rate needed to double an investment.
questions.question: At what annual compound interest rate, compounded annually, will an investment double in \(8\) years? Express the rate as a percentage rounded to two decimal places.
questions.explanation:
Let \(r\) be the annual rate. Doubling means
\[
(1+r)^8=2.
\]
Thus
\[
1+r=2^{\frac{1}{8}}\approx1.0905077,
\]
so
\[
r\approx0.0905=9.05\%.
\]
Therefore the required annual rate is approximately \(9.05\%\).
questions.hint: Set up the equation \((1+r)^8=2\) and solve for \(r\).

questions.learningObjective: Compute the value of an asset after repeated percentage depreciation.
questions.question: A car worth \(30000\text{ USD}\) depreciates by \(15\%\) each year. What is its value after \(3\) years?
questions.explanation:
After each year, the value is multiplied by \(1-0.15=0.85\). After \(3\) years,
\[
30000(0.85)^3=30000(0.614125)=18423.75.
\]
Thus the car is worth \(18423.75\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the original value by \(0.85\) once for each year.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a nominal interest rate with monthly compounding to an effective annual rate.
questions.question: A nominal annual interest rate of \(12\%\) is compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate, expressed as a percentage rounded to two decimal places?
questions.explanation:
The monthly rate is \(0.12/12=0.01\). After twelve monthly compounding periods, the effective annual rate is
\[
\left(1+\frac{0.12}{12}\right)^{12}-1=(1.01)^{12}-1.
\]
Expressed as a percentage, this is
\[
100\bigl((1.01)^{12}-1\bigr)\%\approx12.682503\%.
\]
Rounding the percentage to two decimal places gives \(12.68\%\). The nominal rate \(12.00\%\) does not account for interest earned on earlier interest.

questions.concept: Present Value of an Ordinary Annuity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the present value of a series of equal annual payments.
questions.question: What is the present value of receiving \(500\text{ USD}\) at the end of each year for \(4\) years if the annual interest rate is \(6\%\) compounded annually? Round to the nearest cent.
questions.explanation:
The present value of an ordinary annuity is
\[
\text{PV}=\text{PMT}\frac{1-(1+r)^{-t}}{r}.
\]
Here \(\text{PMT}=500\), \(r=0.06\), and \(t=4\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{PV}&=500\frac{1-(1.06)^{-4}}{0.06} \\
&\approx500\frac{0.207906}{0.06} \\
&\approx1732.55.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the present value is approximately \(1732.55\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Use the present value formula for an ordinary annuity with payments at the end of each year.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the amount owed under quarterly compounding over a fractional number of years.
questions.question: A loan of \(10000\text{ USD}\) has an annual interest rate of \(8\%\) compounded quarterly. If the loan is repaid in one lump sum after \(18\) months, how much is owed? Round to the nearest cent.
questions.explanation:
The quarterly interest rate is
\[
\frac{0.08}{4}=0.02.
\]
The number of quarters in \(18\) months is
\[
4\cdot1.5=6.
\]
Thus the amount owed is
\[
10000(1.02)^6\approx10000(1.126162419)\approx11261.62.
\]
So the amount owed is approximately \(11261.62\text{ USD}\).
questions.hint: Convert the annual rate to a quarterly rate and the time to the number of quarters.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two investment plans using simple and compound interest models.
questions.question: An investor places \(10000\text{ USD}\) in one of two plans for \(10\) years. Plan A earns \(5\%\) interest compounded annually. Plan B earns \(5.1\%\) simple interest annually. Which statement is correct? Round monetary differences to the nearest cent.

options.label: A
options.text: Plan A yields about \(1188.95\text{ USD}\) more than Plan B.

options.label: B
options.text: Plan B yields about \(189.00\text{ USD}\) more than Plan A.

questions.explanation:
For Plan A, the final amount is
\[
10000(1.05)^{10}\approx10000(1.628894626)\approx16288.95.
\]
For Plan B, the final amount is
\[
10000(1+0.051\cdot10)=10000(1.51)=15100.
\]
The difference is
\[
16288.95-15100=1188.95.
\]
Thus Plan A yields about \(1188.95\text{ USD}\) more than Plan B.
questions.hint: Compute the final amount for each plan using the compound interest formula and the simple interest formula, then compare.
